articles.title: NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom Announce Collaboration to Advance Sovereign AI Infrastructure With NVIDIA NVLink Fusion
From Chips to Skills, NVIDIA and Korea Expand Sovereign AI Collaboration

facts.fact: Rebellions plans to adopt NVIDIA NVLink Fusion to connect its next-generation R200 neural processing units to NVIDIA's open infrastructure platform for rack-scale inference.
SK Telecom plans to deploy these systems in its AI data center, including for Korea's 'AI for All' project.
The collaboration is supported by Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT.
The companies plan to use NVIDIA GPUs for prefill and Rebellions NPUs for decode to improve inference throughput and power efficiency.
Rebellions will use the NVIDIA MGX rack architecture for rack-scale system development; Rebellions is developing the R200 NPU for multitrillion-parameter mixture-of-experts models.
Jensen Huang: 'With NVLink Fusion, Korea's chipmakers can connect their custom ASICs to NVIDIA's AI factory platform.'
Sunghyun Park, cofounder and CEO of Rebellions, called Rebellions 'a leading Korean AI silicon startup.'
NVIDIA will use NVIDIA Dynamo software to optimize AI inference with three selected consortia and four leading Korean foundation model builders in Korea's AI for All initiative.

articles.title: Nvidia will investigate CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with possible Chinese spy
Statement from NVIDIA Board of Directors
트럼프 "민주당과 AI 규제 협력할 의사 있어"…중간선거 패배 후 변화
젠슨 황 논란에 엔비디아 침묵…정부 "GPU 공급 차질 없어"
Is Jensen Huang's job on the line? Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld estimates it's 'about a 50-50'
A Message to Our Company

facts.fact: Nvidia's board announced Sunday that it is launching an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation.
A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation.
The board said it has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, but the inquiry will examine all available information.
Huang sent the company a message admitting an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed.
A memo circulating among U.S. policymakers earlier this year claimed Alice Huang had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia's CEO.
Huang wrote: "I was unfaithful to my wife... There is no excuse for what I did."
Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it; the board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.
Earlier Nvidia had said the pair's interactions were 'not unusual' and that it does not share classified information with customers.
Per AI Times (citing Reuters), Trump said he thinks Huang is 'respectable' and said he would be happy to take him on next week's Asia trip.

Nvidia stock fell more than 6% in Frankfurt trading on 9 November to a months-long low, equal to about $270 billion in market value against the 6 November US close; pre-market US trading was about 4% lower.

Vice Minister Ryu Je-myung of Korea's Science Ministry told the National Assembly that already-contracted Nvidia GPUs should arrive on schedule; 10,000 GPUs bought with last year's supplementary budget are already in Korea.
Nvidia officials at Nvidia AI Day Seoul declined to answer questions about Huang, saying they were not related to the event; Madison Huang's Korea visit was cancelled.
Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld put the odds that Huang keeps his job at 'about a 50-50'.
A spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in Washington dismissed the allegations in late October as 'groundless smears and slanders,' and no one has been charged.
Huang's message to staff: 'I was unfaithful to my wife.' and 'NVIDIA's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully.'

stories.title: A private Anthropic model helped a startup, Physical Superintelligence, prove an 18-year-old quantum computing conjecture
stories.first_published_note: Only readable report is AI Times (after cutoff); the original PSI post is from 11-06, so not strictly 'new today'. Caveats in the report: model name unrevealed, whole paper not formally verified.

articles.title: PSI "비공개 앤트로픽 AI로 18년 된 양자 난제 증명"

facts.fact: Physical Superintelligence (PSI) announced on 6 November (US time) that its research system, built on a not-yet-public Anthropic model, produced a full proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, posed in 2008.
PSI's first draft of the proof was done on day three of the research, and it passed verification in Lean, a tool that checks mathematical logic.
PSI launched in the US in September and raised $58 million (about 80 billion won) in seed funding, including from Breakthrough Energy Ventures.
PSI did not disclose the specific model name, how it got access, or its relationship with Anthropic.
The result concerns the number of data lookups, not total computing time; it does not mean quantum computers cannot be faster than classical ones, as Shor's factoring algorithm still shows.
The paper as a whole is not formally verified; experts still need to check that the statement checked by computer matches the original conjecture.
Stanford researchers who reviewed it called it a 'great result' solving a decades-old problem; Stanford researchers had proved part of the conjecture in August.

stories.title: Google DeepMind's AI agents cut the cost of factoring old 1024-bit RSA keys about 30x in theory and replay a 5-month computation in about 4 days
stories.first_published_note: Original is a DeepMind X post (not fetched); AI Times is the only readable report. Not strictly new today.

articles.title: 구글 AI, 구형 RSA 암호 약점 2건 발견…인수분해 비용 30배 낮출 알고리즘 개발

facts.fact: Google DeepMind said on X on 6 November (US time) that AI agents under human supervision produced two results on 1024-bit RSA cryptanalysis.
Two AI agents reproduced a computation from earlier research that took about 5 months in about 4 days using large-scale parallel computing, with about 3.5 times less CPU work.
With only a 32-byte hash value controlled, they found an algorithm theoretically about 1,600 times more efficient than the previous best method.
A new batch-factoring algorithm could, after large precomputation, cut the cost of factoring each additional 1024-bit key by about 30 times versus earlier batch methods.
1024-bit RSA is no longer recommended, and the findings do not affect the security of 2048-bit or larger RSA.
AI Times says OpenAI and Anthropic have also published AI cryptography research results.

articles.title: 오픈AI, 생명과학 AI 벤치마크 공개…GPT-6 아스트라 성능 23%P 향상

facts.fact: OpenAI announced on 6 November (US time) a life-science benchmark, BioBasicsBench, developed with enzyme-design biotech Ligo.
It has 100 tasks across five areas: protein analysis, cell imaging and measurement, quantitative analysis, nucleic acid analysis and molecular cloning.
At 'xhigh' reasoning, GPT-6 Astra scored an average 66.7%, 22.9 percentage points above GPT-5.6 Sol (43.8%) and above GPT-6.1 Sol (62.0%).
Astra used about 4,704 output tokens per task versus 9,099 for GPT-5.6 Sol, about 48% fewer.
OpenAI evaluated seven of its models; the score is average rubric points, not the share of tasks solved perfectly.

articles.title: Tencent AI chief warns of AI biology risks, SCMP reports

facts.fact: Tencent's chief AI scientist Yao Shunyu spoke at a science event in Hong Kong on Saturday, the SCMP reported.
"The cyber abilities of [AI] models and soon [the] bio ability of models will reach a threshold where it's actually possible to do harm," Yao said.
He said Chinese companies that release open models need to take safety very seriously, and that biology risks may be harder to manage than cyber risks.
Yao, 29, joined Tencent last year after a year at OpenAI; Tencent launched its flagship model Hy4 on 4 November.
Tencent said it left material on exploiting software flaws out of Hy4's training data and trained on defensive security data instead.
Tencent said Hy4 has strong basic knowledge of biology but is weaker than leading models at designing experiments, based on internal expert reviews.
Tencent plans to release Hy4's weights and a safety-testing report in the coming days, Reuters reported.
Yao said US firms such as Anthropic make a strong case for keeping top models closed, but argued a mix of open and closed models may work best.

facts.fact: Google has bought Crusoe's data centre site in southeast Wyoming and will build the project itself, Crusoe said on Friday; terms were not disclosed.
It came a day after Google said it would spend $17B on its first Wyoming data centre, in Laramie County.
Crusoe said the sale completes its pre-development work: site selection, governmental approvals and a hybrid power strategy developed with Tallgrass Energy.

Crusoe announced the project with Tallgrass in July 2025, saying it could grow to 10 GW; in June Bloomberg reported Crusoe was being pushed aside after failing to sign customers, with Google raising concerns about costs and timing.
Crusoe says it still has more than 6 GW under contract and over 40 GW in its pipeline, and raised $3.9B at a $30.9B valuation in September.
Google plans a 702 MW fuel-cell power project with US utility AEP, supplied by Bloom Energy, with carbon capture, alongside the existing grid and gas generation.
Voters rejected data centres in 40 of 41 local ballot measures, and several newly elected governors promised to rein in data centres, Bloomberg said.

stories.title: Anthropic shows how 'dreaming' lets Claude agents fix their own wrong memories: Pokemon Red badges 1 to 4, wiki scores 13% to 48%
stories.score_hints: Anthropic blog (Nov 6) original not fetched; AI Times is the only readable source (Korean). Note: two different models compared, so not a clean test; AI Times says so. Same-company caution

articles.title: 앤트로픽, AI가 잘못된 기억 스스로 수정하는 '드리밍' 기술 효과 입증

facts.fact: Anthropic published details on its blog on Nov 6 (US time) of 'Dreaming', where an AI agent reviews past work records and corrects wrong memories when not working; Anthropic first introduced dreaming in May.
In Pokemon Red, Claude Sonnet 3.7 wrote 413 files in 225 folders over about 10,000 steps and earned 1 badge; Claude Fable 5 kept 9 files in 2 folders plus a summary and earned 4 badges.
AI Times notes these are two different models, so the result does not measure memory management alone.
When Claude misremembered a Pokemon Center location and looped, dreaming caught the error by checking logs against memory; the corrected Claude reached the next city and the uncorrected one did not.

Across about 350,000 internal files (420 million tokens), Claude Opus 5 analyzed documents 128 times and built a wiki; wiki-only score rose from 13% to 48%, search-only scored 53%, and search plus wiki rose from 54% to 61%.
Combining search and wiki cut tokens per question by about 20,000; on cross-document acquisition questions wiki accuracy was 87% versus 73% for search only.
In an acquisition-contract task, changing Claude's own memory rules to write one document per contract lifted the legal-document rubric score from 72% to 100%.
Limits: in some legal analysis the wiki made little difference, wikis sometimes grew bigger than the source documents, and reviewing memory costs extra compute.

facts.fact: In a CBS '60 Minutes' interview aired Nov 8 (US time), Trump was asked if he would work with Democrats on AI safety rules and answered 'Of course', adding he is not against having safeguards.
It was his first in-depth interview since Republicans lost both the Senate and the House in the Nov 3 midterms.
He said AI risks are not as serious as people say and can be managed.
He said the US must not fall far behind China because of rules: 'We're number one right now and China doesn't have those safeguards.'
No specific regulation or plan for legislative cooperation with Democrats was given.
The administration has so far preferred industry self-regulation over broad government rules.

articles.title: US Justice Department sets up AI task force

facts.fact: The DOJ set up the Super Intelligence Task Force to lead its work on AI crimes and AI lawsuits, the department said Thursday.
The name follows a September order from Trump telling federal agencies to call AI 'super intelligence' in official documents.
Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward and Associate Deputy Attorney General Stephen Weiss will lead it.
It will go after foreign states, criminal gangs and people or firms that use AI for fraud.
It will absorb the DOJ's AI Litigation Task Force, created in January to challenge state AI laws in federal court, per an internal memo dated 13 October reported by Nextgov.
The DOJ did not say how many staff the task force will have or what it will cost.
